text:
maria: thinking about a phased swap schedule for model version upgrades — want to avoid noisy 1%->100% jumps and also reduce blast radius if quality regresses :thinking_face:
kevin: agree. i'd rather do small plateaus instead of continuous percent increases. gives time for signal to settle. :eyes:
tara: curious — how long are we holding per plateau? metric noise takes a bit to converge for low-traffic cohorts
alex: proposal (sketch):
```
phased_swap:
  cohorts:
    - pct: 1
      hold: 10m
    - pct: 5
      hold: 30m
    - pct: 10
      hold: 1h
    - pct: 25
      hold: 2h
    - pct: 50
      hold: 3h
    - pct: 100
      hold: 0
  abort_if:
    latency_increase_ms: 200
    p50_regression_pct: 2
  telemetry_hooks: ["prompt_set_A", "safety_blocklist_checker"]
```
kevin: +1 to plateaus, but 1% for only 10m seems short for statistical tests. maybe start with 2% for 30m? small cohort sizes mean long tails.
maria: good point. we have a mix of enterprise and small accounts — low pct cohorts might not surface regressions quickly. maybe add a min-sample threshold per cohort before advancing (e.g., 500 requests or 30m whichever later)
tara: also need to clarify what "hold" triggers: purely time, or time+telemetry pass? i'd prefer time+checks so we don't advance if eval alerts fire.
alex: ok updated idea: hold = time OR until sample_count >= N; advance only if all telemetry_checks are green. if any abort condition hit -> immediate rollback to previous stable.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] staged swap initiated by @maria -> v2.1 -> v2.2, starting cohort 1%
kevin: UX thought — console should show per-cohort counters (requests, failures, avg latency, eval score) and a clear "pause/abort" button. teams should be able to tweak the schedule mid-flight.
maria: yes, edit-in-flight is critical. we need two modes: optimistic (auto-advance) and manual (require explicit approve). default to optimistic for self-serve users, manual for enterprise.
tara: what about canary isolation? should cohorts be by customer segments (paid/free) or purely hashed sampling? mixing can hide class-specific regressions.
alex: put segmentation policy in rollout config: sampling_strategy: [hashed_global, segment_by_account_type]. default hashed_global, but allow segment override per rollout.
kevin: final consideration — quota/backpressure interplay. when we increase pct we must ensure routing doesn't break quotas or cold-start spikes. add a pre-check for capacity headroom before each advance.
maria: summary: phased-swap with plateau steps, min-sample gates, telemetry pass/fail checks, segmentation optional, capacity pre-checks, edit-in-flight + manual/auto modes. i'll write a design doc and a short console mock for approvals. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] note: metrics export enabled for this rollout -> prometheus + bigquery for retention 30d
kevin: can you include a small paras on expected SLO impact during each plateau? ops needs it to set temp alerts.
maria: will do — adding to doc now.
